notes.content:
​Hey everyone! I'm still catching up on all the things I need to do this week pertaining to game development, but Episode 2 has officially been released! notes.title: Small quality of life updates
notes.content:
Heya, long time no update for Episode 1. Just wanted to share that I added a bit of polish (mostly features from Episode 2) to the game, as well as slightly improved controller support. Here's the changelog:

-Added left stick axis support for player movement when controller is connected, alongside D-Pad and keyboard controls.

-Changed controls onscreen for tutorials to default to gamepad controls when controller is connected, switches to keyboard when disconnected.

-Added cooldown meters for dashing and Jyl's block.

-Added on screen prompt for when a dialogue is available for an object to interact with.

-Fixed some quirks with room persistence in some sections.

notes.title: Recent Patches
notes.content:
So in my very clearly flawed programmer brain, I will make some dire mistakes sometimes. I just fixed a few with the numerous patches I've put out over the past day or so, because I couldn't even manage to catch them all at once lmao. Here's what I caught and fixed:

-I accidentally had it so even if you did not have the Cipher Wheel, if you selected where it belongs it would open either way. Oops!

-I accidentally forgot to fix a dev cheat where the door in the statue room was open any time the game was loaded, rather than just when it was supposed to be opened. Oops!

-Clarified that you need to attack in close combat, not just hit the aim keys.

To everyone whose experience was affected by these issues, I apologize! I tried to reset the statue room error as best I could, so hopefully it reverts the save as much as possible.

notes.title: Update 4/19/21
notes.content:
This is hopefully the final update of the game save for patches! As always, please let me know if there are bugs because I have been juggling a LOT of code combining this build with the previous build I set live. Here's what's different:
-This build has been optimized by another programmer, and so far on the computers we tested, it runs a lot better! The build that was optimized did not include content made for the 4/4/21 update, so I re-added all the changes I made in that update.
-New hit sounds for a few enemies.
-Resolution in full screen now clearer instead of appearing pixelated on many monitors, as well as mouse hidden in full screen now.
-Skip now enabled for both the Talk dialogues as well as the Bad End dialogue.

And with that we should be done! Now I'll be throwing myself completely back into Episode 2!

notes.title: Update 4/4/2021
notes.content:
Happy Easter! Here is (mostly) the update I had planned that I discussed in my last update announcement. Long story short, all the new content is in the game now, but the optimizations have not been added yet. The deadline for me getting the build back has unfortunately been pushed back a couple weeks, so when I am given the project file I will re-implement the content added in this build and then update again.

So here's what's in this update:

-Improved combat balancing: The difference in Will consumption + damage dealt is now more noticeable in close combat versus normal combat; tutorial textbox explaining close combat added; Will hitbox a bit more precise; Enemies slightly healthier and faster (only faster in close combat); Jyl block slightly stronger.

-Talk feature: Talk to Jyl in order to get clues on where to go/what to do. Because the relevant conversations are now saved/loaded with the game, on first load with older save files, it will default to the first talk conversations regardless of what point you are in, in the save file. In order to use this feature without that hiccup, starting a new save file is recommended, but it will not break older saves. As you proceed through the game in an older save, as relevant conversations pop up they will replace the incorrect ones.

-Bad End 1: A bad end has been added to the game, which will occur if Rina dies with her Will broken.

-A couple of songs have been mixed/mastered by my friend, Percevalko

-A few various bug fixes, such as Ranslug ground spikes breaking if game is paused while they are about to shoot, and the save file playtime glitching/crashing the game when trying to load save files if one was created from the initial demo build from last May.

As always, PLEASE report any bugs/glitches you encounter, as I am a one-woman team and cannot fully test every update myself, even though I try to do whatever I can think of to test things out. If any bugs come up, I'll be releasing smaller updates to fix them leading up to (hopefully) the final update later this month. Thank you everyone for your patience!

notes.title: Update on the Update (Which is Still Very Much Coming)
notes.content:
Hey all! I apologize for the silence on my end after promising a final update to the game. I have gotten new content ready for said update, but having my code optimized by another person with more experience has been taking longer than I originally expected, and I apologize for not planning for that when establishing the original update timeline. However, after touching base with the programmer, we have set March 31st as our solid deadline to have the new code returned to me. Now, I don't expect that I'll be able to update on that day, as there is stuff I need to implement myself into this new version of the game project file, but it does mean that it shouldn't be long after that, that I am able to finally release it. So, as a recap, here's what to expect:
-Better optimization: Overall we are trying to target frame rate and the random crashes. While I'm not sure how this will affect the minimum specs of the game (The specs listed on the store page are the specs of my own computer, because I know it tends to run well on them), it should obviously at least help those who experienced issues.
-Re-balanced combat: As listed in my previous post about the update, I plan to rework the combat stats of the game in order to improve the overall feel and balancing of the game's combat.
-New "Talk" feature: The diary button in the drop-down menu of the pause screen will be replaced with a talk button instead. The diary will still be accessible through selecting the diary in the key item tab, such as how the cipher wheel is opened. The talk window will allow you to talk to Jyl when stuck on what to do, providing a reminder for the current overall goal (exploring, trying to open a door, etc.) as well as more specific puzzle solving goals when faced with a puzzle (hints on what to look out for to solve a puzzle in your current room, explaining what's in the way, etc.) Additionally, while in save rooms, extra small talk dialogue can be triggered if desired.
-Remixed/mastered soundtrack: While the songs themselves will be the same, a friend of mine has offered to fix tracks in the game that could be leveled out better. I am a complete ignoramus when it comes to audio, so basically this is supposed to make the songs hurt your ears less. I make certain tones too loud, what can I say?

I'm really excited to get this update rolled out, so I'm going to do everything in my power to ensure that it comes out as soon as possible. I don't have a solid date for this in case something goes awry, but my goal is the first week or so of April. Will keep everyone posted when that's published, and I want to thank everyone for their patience!

notes.title: Episode 1 Performance Survey
notes.content:
Optimization is on track! However, in order to best ensure the big issues are being tackled, I would appreciate if every player considered taking this survey about their experiences running the game!

https://forms.gle/UGzXQvQC2Yq3bJQp9

Whether or not your experience was buggy, please take the time to fill out this survey! It will allow the final update to this game to come out quicker and be more effective. Thank you!

notes.title: Upcoming support: What to expect
notes.content:
I am planning to make one final major update to this episode, hopefully to be rolled out within a month or less. I am currently talking to programmers in order to see what can be further optimized to make the game as accessible as it can possibly be before I proceed to complete the series. In addition to optimizations, I also plan to make some tweaks to the combat system in order to better balance everything. The changes I plan to make in regards to that include:
-Adding a tutorial window to explain the difference between close combat and regular overworld combat (in the same vein as the tutorials explaining the Will bar and Jyl's block).
-Make close combat use slightly less Will and regular combat use slightly more Will to make a more significant difference between approaches.
-Make close combat inflict more damage on enemies and Rina when one party is hit.
-Make enemies move up more quickly in close combat.
-Any other miscellaneous stat changes I see necessary for balancing when these fixes are made.

Of course, these stat balances are subject to change once I actually get my hands into this, but I will document and report everything I actually do when the update is rolled out. Overall, I do not want to significantly affect the difficulty of the game, but what I do want is to make combat mechanics more meaningful.

On that note, if anyone has any suggestions for stats to be better balanced or what mechanics could be better explained with tutorial windows, please let me know your thoughts and I will consider them! Even if I do not respond to every comment or bit of feedback I get, I always read them, and I spend time consciously thinking about what I read. Thank you to everyone who has given me feedback and reviews so far, I truly appreciate when people take the time to provide their thoughts on my project! :)

notes.title: Optimization Update 12/31/20
notes.content:
Hey all, after being notified about some random game closures and performance issues, I dropped what I was doing to set up Episode 2 and spent hours upon hours optimizing the game where I could. Final product? Still not as optimized as I want but definitely better. Those on the border between proper performance and issues may have the game run better now at least! The two remaining biggest issues are the depth system, which was one of the things I tried the longest to fix but could not change as much as I wanted for now, and the dialogue system, which I trimmed a lot of unused code out of but it could still be a lot better. The problem is that neither of these systems were my original code, so I have to be a lot more careful changing too much or else it could break. Because I have changed a decent amount, please let me know if new bugs have sprung up since!

Changes I made include:

-Putting limits on how many times the game checks the computer's files for save files and preferences

-Reducing the number of fish that appear in rooms

-Slight modification to the depth system

-Removal of unused features/code in the dialogue system

-Made the save rock brighter/more clear

-Cleaned up the main menu code a bit to properly hover on the right options after going back to a previous page
